create.name: Karma Thegsum Chöling Slovakia
create.bio:
Karma Thegsum Chöling Slovakia is a Tibetan Buddhist centre of the Karma Kagyu school in Bratislava, opened in 2013 in a restored early twentieth-century townhouse on Kuzmányho Street. It is one of the centres affiliated with Karma Triyana Dharmachakra, the Karmapa's seat in North America, and is led by the Slovak teacher Lama Sangye. The house holds a large and a small meditation hall, guest rooms and a small stupa, and senior Tibetan teachers such as Tulku Damcho Rinpoche visit to give teachings.

Two evenings a week are open to everyone: on Tuesdays a ritual practice with recitation and mantra, and on Wednesdays silent calm-abiding and compassion meditation followed by a short Buddhist teaching, with instruction for newcomers beforehand. The centre also runs weekend courses and group practice retreats, and people can book a personal retreat of a few days or several months in a room of the house or a dedicated retreat cell. A rural retreat centre, Karma Drupde Ling, is being built at Sobotište in western Slovakia. Teachings are recorded and posted on the centre's YouTube channel, alongside written articles on its site, mostly in Slovak.

courses.title: Amitabha Christmas retreat
courses.description: Three days of group practice of Amitabha, the Buddha of boundless light, with two sessions each day at the Bratislava centre. Open to practitioners who want to deepen this practice over the holidays.

courses.title: Personal meditation retreats
courses.description: Short or long personal retreats, from a few days to several months, in a room of the Bratislava house or in a dedicated secluded retreat room. Retreatants cook for themselves in the shared kitchen and book at least a week ahead.

free_resources.title: Weekly meditation evenings
free_resources.description: Tuesday evenings bring Tibetan Buddhist ritual practice with recitation and mantra; Wednesday evenings offer silent breath-focused meditation, compassion practice and a short teaching, with instruction for newcomers half an hour earlier. In Slovak.

free_resources.title: Guide to calm-abiding (shamatha) meditation
free_resources.description: A written instruction in Slovak on shamatha practice, from building a steady seated posture to resting the attention, posted among the centre's articles and texts.
